adequateGuidanceConfirmed.evidence: The reference already traces delegate self-calls, defaults/bulk dispatch and double application. It distinguishes returning the outer receiver for mutating fluent APIs from preserving a new immutable result.

adequateGuidanceConfirmed.evidence: The reference covers wrapper/delegate identity, equality symmetry/reflexivity, constrained unwrapping, synchronous versus asynchronous failure, throwing observation callbacks, and owned versus borrowed resources including initialization/flush/close failure.
adequateGuidanceConfirmed.consequencePrevented: Treating a dependent stage as transparent, using class inspection as object unwrapping, or closing a still-borrowed/shared resource.
adequateGuidanceConfirmed.disposition: Preserved; no generic lifecycle checklist added.

adequateGuidanceConfirmed.evidence: The retry example checks the budget before each attempt, catches only transient failure, rethrows the final failure and does not sleep afterward. The order section already explains that zero transport calls does not distinguish breaker/retry nesting and requests scripted outcomes with recording boundaries.
adequateGuidanceConfirmed.consequencePrevented: Exhaustion replacing the original failure, unsafe retry classification, or tests passing while the actual composition order remains unproved.
adequateGuidanceConfirmed.technicalEvidence: Unchanged extracted retry passed 28 deterministic checks; outer recording observed one success and inner recording observed two failures then success with the same three delegate calls. Removing only final-attempt rethrow made the same checker fail.
adequateGuidanceConfirmed.disposition: Preserved. The newly created scratch checker is evidence about this example and its own sensitivity, not an existing shipped test or behavioral gain.

adequateGuidanceConfirmed.evidence: Framework composition is conditional on actual ordering/coverage, MVC interceptors are not substituted for the security chain, and RestClient wiring is explicitly Spring 6.1+ with older supported clients preserved.

findings.noChangeRationale: The requested domain lenses already have concrete decision rules, counterexamples and test observations. No supported additional rule justified expanding the package, and no useful capability was removed merely to shorten it.

preserved: Outer-first ordering and the operation/attempt semantics of retry, timeout, breaker, metrics, cache, logging and bulkheads.

Identity/equality/registration behavior and constrained standard unwrapping.

Thread confinement or state synchronization arguments without assuming delegate safety transfers to wrappers.

Owned/borrowed delegate, returned-result and permit lifetimes; failure and close handling.

Functional decoration and adequate simple/no-added-layer alternatives.
Partial per-layer tests and composed-order observations without pretending illustrative timing or load arithmetic is measured.

fixtures.content:
# Export contract
The application uses Java 17. Each export runs on one thread, with no simultaneous access or aliases outside the documented provider lifecycle. The input list and its strings are non-null. There is no mandatory audit sink or additional framework interception.
label mutates the current session and returns that same receiver; it does not create a configured copy. The displayed counter records append calls that returned normally, not bytes persisted or remote acknowledgements. appendAll is intended to count each successful item once, and any delegate failure must remain a failure for the caller. flush is required before the export returns normally. Callers do not use the counting handle after the try block or compare it to the delegate.
Each acquire call returns a fresh session whose ownership transfers to ExportService; the export must close it on normal and exceptional completion.
The provider implementation is supplied by the application adapter and is governed by this approved contract. No other lifecycle transfer occurs. Review the adapter contract before changing the wrapper's lifecycle policy.

fixtures.content:
# Export contract
The application uses Java 17. Each export runs on one thread, with no simultaneous access or aliases outside the documented provider lifecycle. The input list and its strings are non-null. There is no mandatory audit sink or additional framework interception.
label mutates the current session and returns that same receiver; it does not create a configured copy. The displayed counter records append calls that returned normally, not bytes persisted or remote acknowledgements. appendAll is intended to count each successful item once, and any delegate failure must remain a failure for the caller. flush is required before the export returns normally. Callers do not use the counting handle after the try block or compare it to the delegate.
Each acquire call lends the application-owned session for this serial export; ExportService must leave it open on normal and exceptional completion, and the application closes it at shutdown.
The provider implementation is supplied by the application adapter and is governed by this approved contract. No other lifecycle transfer occurs. Review the adapter contract before changing the wrapper's lifecycle policy.

inputs.prerequisites: Use an isolated fixture directory. The four Java source files compile together with javac --release 17; a test can provide a recording SessionProvider/ExportSession, with no external dependencies. Give an actor only this input and normal skill resources, not the handoff or evaluator criteria.

expectedDecisions: Preserve the existing simple decoration when the owned-resource contract is inspected. Forwarding close is correct here; deleting it or refusing ownership without evidence would leak the acquired session.
Verify the default appendAll executes on CountingSession and reaches its append override once per successful item. label must keep returning the wrapper so chained calls retain counting.
Check normal and exceptional paths using a tracking delegate, including exact close count, preserved failure and unchanged successful-item counter. Source inspection alone is not an executed check.
failureConditions: Removing delegate close solely because a decorator is said to borrow by default.
Forwarding appendAll directly to the delegate and losing item-level coverage, or counting at both bulk and item boundaries.
Returning delegate.label(...) and allowing the chain to escape, changing the metric to bytes/durable writes, or introducing unneeded framework/layer changes.

expectedDecisions: Follow the approved provider lifecycle and correct the wrapper/caller close policy locally so the application-owned session stays open after both normal and exceptional export completion.
Do not change the application's final shutdown ownership, counter meaning, flushing requirement, delegate failure classification or Java 17 baseline.

Use a tracking delegate and a later serial borrower to distinguish an open reusable application session from a closed one. Preserve item-level default-method dispatch and wrapper identity in fluent chains.
failureConditions: Keeping unconditional delegate close on the export handle despite the approved borrowed lifetime.
Leaking a newly introduced owned resource, closing the application session from another local finally block, or treating swallowed failures as success.
Fixing lifecycle by bypassing counting, ignoring flush, changing the public interface gratuitously, or assuming thread safety despite the fixture's explicit confinement.

cases.decisiveDifference: Only the ownership sentence in docs/export-contract.md changes: a fresh caller-owned session versus a borrowed application-owned session. Source, counter semantics, caller and thread confinement are identical.
commonCriteria: Inspect the caller and provider contract rather than inferring lifetime from wrapper shape or method name.
Preserve correct simple decoration and inherited default-method coverage; additional layers are not mandatory.
Distinguish proposed checks from executed checks, and do not infer durability, asynchronous cancellation or performance from this synchronous fixture.
cases.walkthrough: Reviewer-only walkthrough: A's try-with-resources forwards close to the owned delegate and is appropriate; B's identical call path closes an application-owned delegate and needs a local ownership-aware correction. Both keep default appendAll dispatch and return-this chaining. These case fixtures were not executed by an actor.
